debate_title: Mandatory pre-deployment safety evaluations for frontier ...

conflicts.point: Whether public compute grants and tiered safety evaluation protocols effectively neutralize regulatory gatekeeping or merely substitute state bureaucratic triage for corporate filtering.

positions.stance: Tiered safety evaluation protocols and public compute allocations neutralize protective moats by shifting verification costs onto public institutions.
Publicly funded compute grants and state-administered allocation mechanisms merely replace corporate gatekeeping with bureaucratic triage that favors established institutions.

conflicts.point: Whether the permanent distribution of open-weight frontier models across global networks justifies mandatory pre-release state oversight despite its chilling effect on permissionless innovation.

positions.stance: Pre-deployment evaluations are mandatory because once frontier model weights are distributed globally, no regulatory authority can retrieve or recall them.
State-managed pre-release gating and compliance queues halt human progress, destroy open-source velocity, and delay vital technological applications.

verdicts.conflict: Whether public compute grants and tiered safety evaluation protocols effectively neutralize regulatory gatekeeping or merely substitute state bureaucratic triage for corporate filtering.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position prevails because it grounds its argument in documented bureaucratic behavior, whereas the safetyist counterargument relies on theoretical mitigation strategies that lack large-scale empirical backing.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence showing that federal compute subsidy programs successfully distribute resources to independent open-source developers at rates proportional to commercial incumbents.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the permanent distribution of open-weight frontier models across global networks justifies mandatory pre-release state oversight despite its chilling effect on permissionless innovation.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position holds greater weight because it correctly identifies the irreversibility of global model weight diffusion, a technical reality that permanent open-source distribution protocols cannot recall once deployed.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrated technical mechanisms capable of securely recalling or disabling frontier model weights after public distribution across global peer-to-peer networks.
